headline_findings.title: Bearer Tokens & OAuth 2.0 Eclipse Legacy Auth (79% & 51%)
headline_findings.summary: Bearer tokens (personal access tokens/API tokens) are the single most prevalent authentication mechanism across the 100 apps (79 apps), followed closely by OAuth 2.0 (51 apps). Legacy static API keys are rapidly being deprecated (e.g., Airtable sunset in 2024, HubSpot private apps).

headline_findings.title: 77% of Apps Are Self-Serve Developer Friendly
headline_findings.summary: 77 out of 100 apps allow developers to acquire test credentials immediately without human interaction (49 free tier, 28 free trial). Only 23% require paid plans, compliance approval, or commercial sales gates.

headline_findings.title: Developer & Productivity Lead Self-Serve; Finance & Enterprise Lag
headline_findings.summary: 100% of Developer/Infra tools and 100% of Productivity tools are self-serve. In contrast, Finance (40% gated) and CRM (20% gated) suffer from compliance reviews, bank KYC, and institutional contracts.

headline_findings.title: Huge MCP White-Space Opportunity (66% Have No MCP)
headline_findings.summary: Only 6% of apps have official MCP servers and 28% have community MCP servers. 66% of apps have ZERO MCP implementations, creating an open market opportunity for Composio to launch first-party toolkits for high-demand tools like Plaid, Close, Plain, and Ramp.

headline_findings.title: The Three Integration Traps: CLIs, Ghost APIs, and Approval Walls
headline_findings.summary: Not all 'apps' are SaaS APIs. Sherlock and Mermaid CLI are local command-line tools requiring shell subagents. fanbasis and Consensus have zero public REST APIs. Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, and Amazon SP-API require strict developer vetting before production.
